text.p: STOCKHOLM - Swedish telecommunications group AB LM Ericsson on Tuesday rang up a 33 percent jump in pre-tax profits in 1996 with its mobile phone unit continuing to show sound growth and an improved performance by its public telecommunications unit.
The pre-tax profit of 10.15 billion crowns ($1.4 billion) was slightly higher than a market forecast of 10.03 billion crowns despite the stronger crown wiping 900 million crowns off the result.
"The result was reasonably encouraging and our initial reaction is positive," Simon Street, BZW analyst told Reuters.
In anticipation of the report, Ericsson's share price rose eight crowns on Monday but once the earnings were released it slipped back three crowns to 249 crowns.

"People were long in the share before the report so there is no real upside," one Stockholm trader said. "But there was nothing negative in the report and the share price could swing several times later today."
Ericsson said turnover for the year rose 26 percent to 124.27 billion crowns while its order bookings climbed 31 percent to 138.05 billion crowns.
Ericsson said its radio communications continued to show strong growth in mobile telephones, its main business area.
Order bookings rose 31 percent to 84.21 billion crowns and turnover by 40 percent to 79.10 billion crowns.
"The trend of business for mobile telecommunications systems has continued to be very favourable," Ericsson said.
"The growth in the number of subscribers, for digitial systems in particular, is very rapid throughout the world."
It repeated an estimate that the number of mobile phone subscribers rose to 137 million in 1996, a jump of 50 million, and that it expected 590 million subscribers in five years.
In its second largest division, public communications, order bookings rose 56 percent to 33.04 billion crowns, largely due to orders from Brazil.
"The business area as a whole shows weak but improved profitability. The process of change, designed to shorten lead times and reduce costs, is continuing," Ericsson said.
Analysts said the strong order bookings were convincing.
"Particularly public telecommunications show a strong order intake, while radio communications' order intake also was strong," said Ulf Hellzen, Swedbank analyst.
He said the increased dividend of 2.50 crowns a share from 1.75 crowns was a positive signal.
Ericsson said orders for AXE systems used in fixed networks rose 18 percent.
"This represents a major success, condering the heavy pressure on prices in this market," Ericsson said.
Ericsson said its gross margins weakened.

"Gross margins have weakened as a result of increased competition, currency effects and increased risks which have been taken into account in the report concerning changes in technology and markets," Ericsson said.
Ericsson's deputy managing director, CW Ros said there was no signs of an end to the price pressures experienced in 1996.
"I would not be surprised if it was about the same as last year," Ros told a news conference.
"We have no signs that point to anything else."
($ = 7.392 Swedish Crowns)
